paragraphs: Alertus Technologies sells emergency notification hardware and software that organizations install to warn everyone on a site at once. The company positions itself as a single source for mass emergency notification systems and critical communication needs. Its stated goal is to help colleges and universities, K-12 schools, corporations and government organizations solve unified mass notification problems.

The approach is network based, using an organization's existing IP network to turn VoIP phones into alerting devices. Hardware fills the gaps, including a wall-mounted alerting device meant for places with no existing notification endpoints. Outdoor coverage is handled by high power speaker arrays.

The company traces its origin to 2001, when an F3 tornado ripped through the University of Maryland campus. Alertus was founded the following year. It reports serving more than 2,500 organizations across more than 40 countries. Those customers are described as spanning higher education, K-12, industrial, corporate, healthcare, government and military sectors.
